meta.scope: Indonesia Batch 8 — Maritime & fisheries statistics, selected Java municipal nodes (Magelang, Malang — historical continuity places), and general government / fiscal accounts. Continues the dig while recognising the archipelagic and historical depth of the territory.
meta.note: User family connection: great-grandfather P.K.W. Lakeman served as Burgemeester in Magelang (1929–1934) and Malang (1933–1936) in the Dutch East Indies. These places remain active statistical units under modern BPS local offices.

candidates.title: Statistics of Marine and Coastal Resources
candidates.description: Annual BPS publication on the potential and management of marine and coastal resources. Framed around blue-economy, climate adaptation and sustainable coastal prosperity themes aligned with long-term national planning.
candidates.notes: Core maritime-resource statistical product for the world’s largest archipelagic state.

candidates.title: Statistics of Fishing Ports
candidates.description: Annual statistics on the number, class and activity of fishing ports, fish-auction facilities and related catch volumes handled through ports. Aceh and other provinces feature prominently in port counts.
candidates.notes: Infrastructure and production node for the capture-fisheries sector.

candidates.title: Fisheries production statistics (capture and aquaculture)
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries related
candidates.description: Official statistics on fish catch and aquaculture production. Indonesia ranks among the world’s largest fisheries producers; the series is central to food security, exports and coastal livelihoods.
candidates.notes: Primary production node for the maritime food economy.

candidates.title: Kota Magelang / Kabupaten Magelang local statistics (Dalam Angka)
candidates.publisher: BPS Kota Magelang / BPS Kabupaten Magelang
candidates.description: Annual ‘Dalam Angka’ (in figures) publications for Magelang City and Magelang Regency. Standard local statistical yearbooks covering population, labour, social, economic and regional-account indicators. Magelang sits in the Central Java highland corridor.
candidates.notes: Local node with historical continuity. Magelang was a Dutch East Indies administrative posting; it remains an active BPS statistical unit today.

candidates.title: Kota Malang / Kabupaten Malang local statistics (Dalam Angka)
candidates.publisher: BPS Kota Malang / BPS Kabupaten Malang
candidates.description: Annual local statistical yearbooks for Malang City and Malang Regency. Malang is a major East Java urban and educational centre in a highland agricultural region.
referenced_by: Education, tourism and local economic analysis
candidates.notes: Local node with historical continuity. Malang was a Dutch East Indies burgemeester posting; it remains a significant modern urban statistical unit.

candidates.title: Selected Java municipal statistical system (Dalam Angka series)
candidates.description: The widespread local ‘Dalam Angka’ yearbook system that produces city- and regency-level statistical compendia across Java and the rest of Indonesia. Provides the granular municipal layer beneath provincial PDRB and population series.
candidates.notes: System-level node for the dense local statistical production that characterises modern Indonesia.

candidates.title: General Government Accounts of Indonesia
candidates.description: Detailed general-government accounts (central and regional) following the sequence of national-accounts tables: production, generation and allocation of income, secondary distribution, use of disposable income, and capital account.
candidates.notes: Institutional-sector densification of the public-finance cluster.

candidates.title: State Budget (APBN) realization and fiscal statistics
candidates.description: Official realization statistics for the State Budget (APBN) — revenues (tax and non-tax), expenditures, deficit/surplus and financing. High-frequency monitoring product central to fiscal policy communication.

candidates.title: Blue-economy policy and statistical framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS marine statistics, RPJPN/RPJMN and maritime policy documents
candidates.description: Recurring policy and statistical framing of the ‘blue economy’ that organises marine-resource, fisheries, coastal and climate-adaptation data under a long-term development narrative (including Golden Indonesia 2045).
candidates.notes: Policy-frame node for the maritime cluster.

candidates.title: Indonesia maritime–local–fiscal densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS marine, local and government-account sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding marine/coastal resources, fishing ports, fisheries production, selected Java municipal yearbooks (Magelang, Malang), the broader Dalam Angka local system, general government accounts, APBN fiscal statistics and blue-economy framing.
referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier Java-core, environmental and national-accounts series
